# Examples from paper

The following examples come from (paper reference?) in section 5. Let $p_A = \frac{N_A}{N}$, $n_A = \sum_{h=1}^H n_h \alpha_h$.

## Example (i)
In example i, we assume that the domain exists in only one stratum, without loss of generality, the first stratum. This yields an upper bound on the relative bias:

$$\mbox{RelBias} \leq \frac{p_A^2}{n_A\sigma_1^2/\mu_1^2}$$
```{r load_package}
library(SDR)
```

```{r prep, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
set.seed(2020)
H <- 4

parmlst1 <- list(
  Nh = rep(1000, H),
  nh = rep(15, H),
  muh = c(2, rnorm(H - 1, 9)),
  sigmah = c(1, sample(c(0.5, 1, 2), H - 1, replace=TRUE)),
  alphah = c(0.05, rep(0, H-1))
)

parmlst2 <- list(
  Nh = rep(1000, H),
  nh = rep(c(5,15), length=H),
  muh = rep(10, H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.5, H)
)

parmlst3 <- list(
  Nh = rep(1000, H),
  nh = rep(5, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(1,5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.5, H)
)

parmlst4_1 <- list(
  Nh = rep(10000, H),
  nh = rep(5, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(1,5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.01, H)
)

parmlst4_2 <- list(
  Nh = rep(10000, H),
  nh = rep(5, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(1,5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.04, H)
)

parmlst4_3 <- list(
  Nh = rep(10000, H),
  nh = rep(5, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(1,5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.06, H)
)

parmlst4_4 <- list(
  Nh = rep(10000, H),
  nh = rep(5, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(1,5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(0.08, H)
)

H <- 8

parmlst5 <- list(
  Nh = rep(1000, H),
  nh = rep(100, length=H),
  muh = rep(c(0.5, 1.5), length=H),
  sigmah = rep(1, H),
  alphah = rep(c(0.6, 0, 0.8, 0), length=H)
)

```

We generate a small population of 4 strata 
```{r example1}
print(parmlst1)

p_A <- (parmlst1$Nh/sum(parmlst1$Nh))[1]
n_A <- parmlst1$nh[1]*p_A
sigma_1 <- parmlst1$sigmah[1]
mu_1 <- parmlst1$muh[1]

print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst1)$RelBias)
print(p_A^2/(n_A*sigma_1^2/mu_1^2))

```
We can see that this upper bound can be somewhat large especially as $\alpha_1$ grows.

## Example (ii)
Here we have $H$ is even and all terms are constant except the sample size values which alternate between two values, $n_h = (n/H) \cdot (1 + (-1)^h \rho)$, where $\rho \in (0, 1)$. We can approximate the relative bias as 

$$H\cdot \frac{p_A^2}{n_A(\sigma_1^2/\mu_1^2 + 1 - p_A)} \left( \frac{2\rho^2}{1-\rho^2} \right)$$

```{r example2}
print(parmlst2)

rho <- with(parmlst2, (max(nh) - min(nh))* length(nh)/(2*sum(nh)) )
H <- length(parmlst2$nh)
p_A <- parmlst2$Nh[1]/sum(parmlst2$Nh)
n_A <- parmlst2$nh[1]*parmlst2$alphah[1]
sigma_1 <- parmlst2$sigmah[1]
mu_1 <- parmlst2$muh[1]

print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst2)$RelBias)
print(H*(p_A^2/(n_A*(sigma_1^2/mu_1^2 + 1 - p_A)) *((2*rho^2)/(1 - rho^2))))
```
## Example (iii)

Example iii switches the term that alternates from $n_h$ to $\mu_h$ in a similar alternation between two values. The relative bias is then approximated as 

$$H \cdot \frac{2 \rho^2 p_A^2}{n_A (\sigma_1^2\mu^2 + (1- p_A)*(1+\rho^2))} $$

```{r example3}
print(parmlst3)

H <- length(parmlst3$nh)
p_A <- parmlst3$Nh[1]/sum(parmlst3$Nh)
n_A <- parmlst3$nh[1]*parmlst3$alphah[1]
sigma_1 <- parmlst3$sigmah[1]
mu <- sum(parmlst3$muh*parmlst3$Nh)/sum(parmlst3$Nh)
rho <- with(parmlst3, (max(muh) - min(muh))/(2*mu))


print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst3)$RelBias)
print((2*rho^2*p_A^2)/(n_A*(sigma_1^2/mu^2 + (1-p_A)*(1+rho^2))))
```

## Example (iv)
Here we explore the approximate linearity of the relative bias under small domains as a function of the small domain size.

```{r example4_1}
print(parmlst4_1)
print(parmlst4_2)
print(parmlst4_3)
print(parmlst4_4)

print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_1)$RelBias)
print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_2)$RelBias)
print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_3)$RelBias)
print(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_4)$RelBias)


X <- data.frame(x=c(parmlst4_1$alphah[1], 
       parmlst4_2$alphah[1], 
       parmlst4_3$alphah[1],
       parmlst4_4$alphah[1]),
       y= c(SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_1)$RelBias,
     SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_2)$RelBias,
     SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_3)$RelBias,
     SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst4_4)$RelBias))
plot(X$x,
     X$y
     )
m1 <- lm(data=X, y~x)
abline(m1)

```
## Example (v)

In example v, we have a situation where the relative bias will not become arbitrarily small with larger domain size as can be seen below.
```{r example5}
print(parmlst5)

H <- length(parmlst5$Nh)
nh_seq <- c(10, 50, 100)

relbias_ans <- sapply(nh_seq, function(n){
  parmlst <- parmlst5
  parmlst$nh <- rep(n, H)
  
  SDR::PermRelBias(parmlst)$RelBias
})

plot(nh_seq, relbias_ans)
```
